run.residualRisk: The TV203/Free Vision closure is locally ready, but Terminal.GUI has not yet been audited and exact-head remote delivery evidence remains pending.
run.followUp: Deliver the exact Feature-028 head, then run Feature 029 and its findings-derived closure before Wave 5; keep Wave 6 blocked through the post-Wave-5 delta review.
run.reevaluationTrigger: A canonical Feature-024 contract, finding, resolution, protected consumer, proof method, or acceptance workflow changes.

findingClosures.originalObservation: CreateMouse accepts composite mouse masks instead of requiring one concrete mouse event kind.
findingClosures.redProof: Build 215 rejected the pre-fix composite-kind behavior.
findingClosures.historicalIntent: Typed event channels: Events carry one active channel, numeric commands keep stable identity, and dispatch stops after explicit consumption.
findingClosures.apiImpact: None; Feature 028 revalidates the existing public event factory without changing it.
findingClosures.a11yImpact: Concrete event kinds keep keyboard and pointer dispatch deterministic.
findingClosures.platformImpact: Managed event construction is platform-neutral; raw host ingress is covered by R-028-001.
findingClosures.residualRisk: A future factory or event-kind expansion could weaken the one-concrete-kind invariant.
findingClosures.followUp: None while all public event factories retain the same invariant.
findingClosures.reevaluationTrigger: A public event factory or concrete event-kind set changes.

findingClosures.originalObservation: Focus transfer is not coupled to child validation, so an invalid input can lose focus without a rejection boundary.
findingClosures.redProof: Build 219 failed because no validator-owned focus-release contract existed.
findingClosures.historicalIntent: Focus transition: Groups own children, maintain one current view, propagate state, and release children in defined order.
findingClosures.apiImpact: None in Feature 028; the additive focus result from Feature 025 is revalidated.
findingClosures.a11yImpact: Rejected focus transfer preserves input and keeps the accessible current control stable.
findingClosures.residualRisk: New focus owners could bypass the validation-aware transfer path.
findingClosures.followUp: None while all focus changes use the group-owned transition contract.
findingClosures.reevaluationTrigger: Focus ownership, eligibility, validation, or announcement ordering changes.

findingClosures.originalObservation: TGroup propagates Focused and Disabled uniformly to every child instead of applying state-specific hierarchy rules.
findingClosures.redProof: Build 221 exposed uniform Focused and Disabled propagation plus missing Dragging inheritance.
findingClosures.historicalIntent: Hierarchy and state propagation: Groups own children, maintain one current view, propagate state, and release children in defined order.
findingClosures.apiImpact: None in Feature 028; state-specific propagation remains the accepted Feature-025 behavior.
findingClosures.a11yImpact: Exactly one current and focused descendant keeps focus announcements coherent.
findingClosures.residualRisk: A new state flag could be assigned the wrong hierarchy responsibility.
findingClosures.followUp: None for the current closed state set.
findingClosures.reevaluationTrigger: Group state propagation or insertion inheritance changes.

findingClosures.originalObservation: The application loop has no bounded pending-event and Idle lifecycle contract.
findingClosures.redProof: Build 223 failed because pending-event, idle, CPU-release, and nonblocking input seams were absent.
findingClosures.historicalIntent: Application loop: The program loop obtains and dispatches events, the desktop owns windows, and modal execution returns one command result.
findingClosures.apiImpact: None in Feature 028; the bounded pending-event and idle seams are only revalidated.
findingClosures.a11yImpact: Input remains ahead of idle work, preventing delayed keyboard handling.
findingClosures.platformImpact: Non-busy managed polling must remain deterministic on all supported hosts.
findingClosures.residualRisk: A host adapter could reintroduce busy waiting or idle-before-input ordering.
findingClosures.followUp: Recheck through the cross-platform CI matrix.
findingClosures.reevaluationTrigger: Event polling, pending storage, idle scheduling, or shutdown changes.

findingClosures.originalObservation: Desktop ownership exists, but insertion, top-window, tile, cascade, and close-all contracts are not available or proven as one coherent stack model.
findingClosures.redProof: Build 228 failed because the coherent Desktop stack and operation-result API was absent.
findingClosures.historicalIntent: Desktop and window stack: The program loop obtains and dispatches events, the desktop owns windows, and modal execution returns one command result.
findingClosures.apiImpact: None in Feature 028; accepted desktop operations are revalidated without extension.
findingClosures.a11yImpact: Focus-preserving stack operations keep keyboard navigation predictable.
findingClosures.platformImpact: Desktop geometry uses managed bounds and is host-independent.
findingClosures.residualRisk: Future mixed child types could weaken stack or geometry assumptions.
findingClosures.followUp: None for the current desktop child contracts.
findingClosures.reevaluationTrigger: Desktop Z-order, focus, geometry, or close-all policy changes.

findingClosures.originalObservation: Default keyboard close stops at a cmClose signal and the framework lacks a complete modal execution lifecycle with result and focus restoration.
findingClosures.redProof: Build 230 failed because explicit close decisions and owner-scoped modal execution were absent.
findingClosures.historicalIntent: Modality and window close: The program loop obtains and dispatches events, the desktop owns windows, and modal execution returns one command result.
findingClosures.apiImpact: None in Feature 028; close and modal result contracts remain unchanged.
findingClosures.a11yImpact: Keyboard close, modal isolation, and focus restoration are primary acceptance boundaries.
findingClosures.platformImpact: Managed lifecycle semantics must agree across supported hosts.
findingClosures.residualRisk: New owners or exception paths could skip modal cleanup or focus restoration.
findingClosures.followUp: None while owner-scoped cleanup remains centralized.
findingClosures.reevaluationTrigger: Close validation, modal ownership, result, cleanup, or focus restoration changes.

findingClosures.originalObservation: Commands have per-item Enabled flags but no shared command-state contract refreshed from active context.
findingClosures.redProof: Build 226 failed because no shared opt-in command-state provider or immutable context existed.
findingClosures.historicalIntent: Status and command enablement: Menus navigate enabled entries, status definitions expose executable commands, and keyboard shortcuts remain visible.
findingClosures.apiImpact: None in Feature 028; the existing immutable command context is revalidated.
findingClosures.a11yImpact: Menu, status, and keyboard command availability remain synchronized.
findingClosures.residualRisk: A new dispatch trigger could omit command-state refresh.
findingClosures.followUp: None for current trigger set; remote proof covers all hosts.
findingClosures.reevaluationTrigger: Command providers, refresh triggers, presentation overlays, or dispatch policy changes.

findingClosures.originalObservation: The real TProgram console path bypasses TKeyCodeTranslator for most keys and disagrees with TWindow about modifier bit values.
findingClosures.redProof: Build 217 proved raw printable and Ctrl input diverged from the canonical translator.
findingClosures.historicalIntent: Keyboard translation: Keyboard and mouse input are normalized into events; click, double-click, drag, and fallback paths remain ordered.
findingClosures.apiImpact: None in Feature 028; the canonical translator path remains unchanged.
findingClosures.a11yImpact: Printable, navigation, Alt, Ctrl, Shift, and fallback keys reach one keyboard path.
findingClosures.platformImpact: Exact-head Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows execution is required because host key input differs.
findingClosures.residualRisk: Unsupported host key sequences remain outside the bounded ConsoleKeyInfo contract.
findingClosures.followUp: Re-evaluate when console ingress or supported terminal protocols change.
findingClosures.reevaluationTrigger: Console ingress, key translation, modifier bits, or platform adapters change.

findingClosures.originalObservation: The framework proves title-bar drag only and has no generic tracked drag session for list and file drag-and-drop.
findingClosures.redProof: Build 234 failed because generic drag target, state, session, and result contracts were absent.
findingClosures.historicalIntent: Activation, drag, and fallback: Keyboard and mouse input are normalized into events; click, double-click, drag, and fallback paths remain ordered.
findingClosures.apiImpact: None in Feature 028; the generic drag contracts remain unchanged.
findingClosures.a11yImpact: Pointer and keyboard paths must reach equivalent bounded results and cancellation.
findingClosures.platformImpact: Pointer capability is conditional; the keyboard fallback remains available on every host.
findingClosures.residualRisk: Wave-6 application policy and destructive drop outcomes remain product work.
findingClosures.followUp: Wave 6 may compose the shared session only after Feature 029 and Wave-5 delta review.
findingClosures.reevaluationTrigger: Drag capture, threshold, target negotiation, keyboard parity, or lifecycle cancellation changes.

findingClosures.originalObservation: TDialog handles every command as a completion request and standard Valid does not validate child controls.
findingClosures.redProof: Build 246 failed because explicit validation phases/results and a bounded completion classifier were absent.
findingClosures.historicalIntent: Dialog state and validation: Dialogs preserve control state, validate before acceptance, and controls consume activation and editing input predictably.
findingClosures.apiImpact: None in Feature 028; additive validation result and classifier contracts are revalidated.
findingClosures.a11yImpact: The first rejection retains focus and exposes text-first evidence; Cancel remains reachable.
findingClosures.residualRisk: A derived completion classifier could expand commands without matching validation policy.
findingClosures.followUp: None while classifier extensions remain bounded and tested.
findingClosures.reevaluationTrigger: Dialog completion classification, validation order, rejection focus, or cancellation policy changes.

findingClosures.originalObservation: TInputLine and TValidator are separate APIs without an attachment, transfer, focus-loss, or acceptance integration contract.
findingClosures.redProof: Build 248 failed because TInputLine had no phase-aware validator, selection, or observable result contract.
findingClosures.historicalIntent: Selection, input, and color: Dialogs preserve control state, validate before acceptance, and controls consume activation and editing input predictably.
findingClosures.apiImpact: None in Feature 028; phase-aware validator and state contracts are revalidated.
findingClosures.a11yImpact: Rejected edits and focus loss preserve text, cursor, selection, focus, and readable rejection.
findingClosures.platformImpact: Input validation is platform-neutral after event normalization.
findingClosures.residualRisk: A new mutation path could bypass candidate-before-state validation.
findingClosures.followUp: None for current edit, focus, and acceptance phases.
findingClosures.reevaluationTrigger: Input mutation, selection, focus release, validator phase, or acceptance integration changes.

findingClosures.originalObservation: File-dialog completion does not prove mode-aware validation for wildcard, directory, missing open target, and save target cases.
findingClosures.redProof: Build 250 failed because the closed mode-aware outcome and observable rejection contracts were absent.
findingClosures.historicalIntent: File selection and conflicts: Editors mutate buffers, clipboard commands preserve text, file dialogs separate selection from I/O, and close paths protect modified data.
findingClosures.apiImpact: None in Feature 028; typed outcomes and metadata-only classification remain unchanged.
findingClosures.a11yImpact: Invalid paths and wildcards produce text-first rejection without losing dialog state.
findingClosures.platformImpact: Tests use temporary owned paths; host-specific path behavior remains covered by the runtime matrix.
findingClosures.residualRisk: Callers still own later I/O and TOCTOU policy after an accepted metadata decision.
findingClosures.followUp: Wave consumers must keep destructive I/O outside the dialog classifier.
findingClosures.reevaluationTrigger: File-dialog mode, metadata classification, history publication, or caller I/O ownership changes.

findingClosures.originalObservation: Named resources are proven for help and dialog descriptions, but not for reconstructible menu, status-line, and dialog composition.
findingClosures.redProof: Builds 252 and 253 failed because menu/status models, primitive records, factories, and built-in registrations were absent.
findingClosures.historicalIntent: Resources and localization: Help resolves contexts and references, resources use named lookup, history is ordered, and localized text has explicit fallback.
findingClosures.apiImpact: None in Feature 028; closed primitive records and allowlisted factories are revalidated.
findingClosures.a11yImpact: Menu and status descriptions retain visible text, stable order, commands, and accessible shortcuts.
findingClosures.platformImpact: System.Text.Json records and exact keys are platform-neutral; generated binary compatibility is not claimed.
findingClosures.residualRisk: Future registrations or parser limits could weaken allowlisting or atomic rejection.
findingClosures.followUp: No historical binary compatibility or arbitrary runtime activation is accepted.
findingClosures.reevaluationTrigger: Resource registry, description format, parser limits, semantic validation, or runtime reconstruction changes.

integrationSlices.title: Raw keyboard, concrete event kind, command, and dispatch path
integrationSlices.assertions: Raw function and unknown keys retain scan-code semantics; Ctrl remains distinct from Alt; one concrete event kind enters dispatch; command routing and consumption happen exactly once; keyboard close reaches visible lifecycle state.
integrationSlices.negativeOrFallback: Unknown keys use scan code zero without fabricating a command; composite event masks are rejected; consumed events skip later dispatch phases.
integrationSlices.helperRole: PrimaryProof: every cited test enters a maintained production boundary; the Feature-028 validator only checks evidence integrity.
integrationSlices.proofLimit: This slice does not claim native terminal protocol parity or start any Wave-5/Wave-6 consumer.
integrationSlices.platforms: Local managed proof plus exact-head Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows CI; WSL remains N/A without a dedicated runner.
integrationSlices.a11yEvidence: Keyboard command and Alt-menu activation remain reachable, distinguish modifiers, and expose deterministic visible state.
integrationSlices.residualRisk: Host terminals may report unsupported key sequences outside the bounded ConsoleKeyInfo contract.
integrationSlices.followUp: Re-evaluate in terminal ingress features when the supported raw protocol changes.
integrationSlices.reevaluationTrigger: Console translation, modifier mapping, event dispatch, command routing, or event-consumption behavior changes.

integrationSlices.title: Atomic focus, hierarchy state, validation veto, and accessible announcement
integrationSlices.productionEntry: TGroup.TrySetFocus -> TView.CanReleaseFocus -> TInputLine validation -> owner state and program focus broadcast
integrationSlices.assertions: Focus transfer is atomic; a validator veto preserves text, cursor, selection, current view, and focus; state-specific propagation keeps one focused descendant; a successful desktop transition reaches the program broadcast.
integrationSlices.negativeOrFallback: Ineligible or invalid targets reject transfer without partial state change; owner-local Disabled state and inserted-child inheritance remain distinct.
integrationSlices.helperRole: PrimaryProof: real group, view, input, desktop, and program ownership paths execute; the evidence validator only resolves their references.
integrationSlices.proofLimit: This slice does not redesign focus visuals or add pointer-only focus behavior.
integrationSlices.platforms: Managed focus and validation are platform-neutral; exact-head OS runs guard host integration.
integrationSlices.a11yEvidence: Invalid input retains focus and successful focus changes publish the text-oriented program signal.
integrationSlices.residualRisk: A new focus owner or state flag could bypass the established ordering.
integrationSlices.followUp: None while all focus changes remain group-owned and validation-aware.
integrationSlices.reevaluationTrigger: Focus ownership, validator release, state responsibility, or focus-broadcast behavior changes.

integrationSlices.title: Pending event, idle ordering, command refresh, CPU release, and shutdown
integrationSlices.productionEntry: TProgram.Run -> GetEvent pending slot/input -> HandleEvent -> Idle/command-state refresh -> shutdown
integrationSlices.assertions: One bounded pending event drains before new input; input precedes idle; idle yields CPU and stops after shutdown; command state refreshes on all accepted triggers and stale dispatch is rejected.
integrationSlices.negativeOrFallback: A full pending slot cannot be overwritten; idle cannot displace queued input; shutdown ends later idle work.
integrationSlices.helperRole: PrimaryProof: tests execute the real TProgram run and event lifecycle; scheduling fakes only provide deterministic host input.
integrationSlices.proofLimit: This slice does not require background threads or reproduce a native message pump.
integrationSlices.platforms: Managed ordering is local; exact-head Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows execute the same CI command body.
integrationSlices.a11yEvidence: Keyboard input remains ahead of idle work and command availability stays synchronized.
integrationSlices.residualRisk: A future host adapter could add an unbounded queue or busy wait outside TProgram.
integrationSlices.followUp: Revalidate through every supported runtime job when input polling changes.
integrationSlices.reevaluationTrigger: Pending storage, event polling, idle scheduling, command refresh, or shutdown changes.

integrationSlices.title: Desktop stack, close, modal, application, view-tree, and cell lifecycle
integrationSlices.productionEntry: TApplication.Run -> TDesktop stack -> TWindow close or TDialog.ExecuteModal -> owner cleanup and focus restoration
integrationSlices.assertions: Desktop order, bounds, selection, close-all outcomes, visible close affordance, owner-scoped modal result, view removal, rendered-cell clearing, cleanup, and focus restoration remain coherent through real application lifecycle.
integrationSlices.negativeOrFallback: Close veto preserves the view; same-owner modal reentry is rejected; exceptions and shutdown still clean modal state; empty desktop operations are deterministic no-ops.
integrationSlices.helperRole: PrimaryProof: desktop, window, dialog, and application methods execute maintained production ownership and rendering paths.
integrationSlices.proofLimit: This slice does not add application-specific windows or native nested message loops.
integrationSlices.platforms: Managed ownership and rendering are cross-platform; exact-head runtime jobs check host composition.
integrationSlices.a11yEvidence: Keyboard close, visible affordance, modal isolation, and previous-focus restoration are asserted.
integrationSlices.residualRisk: New desktop child kinds or modal owners could require additional lifecycle proof.
integrationSlices.followUp: None for the current framework-owned stack and modal contracts.
integrationSlices.reevaluationTrigger: Desktop ordering, geometry, close policy, modal ownership, rendering, or focus restoration changes.

integrationSlices.title: Bounded drag capture, target, cancellation, rendering, and keyboard parity
integrationSlices.productionEntry: TProgram pointer/key event -> TWindow/TDragSession -> IDragTarget -> rendered final or restored state
integrationSlices.assertions: One-cell threshold creates one capture; bounds and target negotiation are explicit; pointer and keyboard commit equivalent positions and rendered regions; terminal result is immutable.
integrationSlices.negativeOrFallback: Escape, capability loss, disable, removal, shutdown, unsupported mouse, rejected target, and invalid start restore or preserve state and clear capture.
integrationSlices.helperRole: PrimaryProof: actual application and window loops execute; synthetic events only provide deterministic input.
integrationSlices.proofLimit: This slice does not define Wave-6 destructive copy, move, delete, trash, or full desktop drag-and-drop policy.
integrationSlices.platforms: Pointer support is capability-based; keyboard fallback is mandatory on every platform.
integrationSlices.a11yEvidence: Keyboard move mode reaches the same bounded result and remains available when mouse support is disabled or unsupported.
integrationSlices.residualRisk: Future drag targets may add product policy beyond the shared session.
integrationSlices.followUp: Wave 6 owns destructive operation decisions; shared session drift blocks earlier.
integrationSlices.reevaluationTrigger: Drag capture, threshold, target, result, lifecycle cancellation, rendering, or keyboard fallback changes.

integrationSlices.title: Dialog completion, ordered validation, state preservation, and accessible rejection
integrationSlices.productionEntry: TDialog.HandleEvent -> completion classifier -> ordered child validation -> TInputLine validator phase -> focus/result
integrationSlices.assertions: Only accepted completion commands close; validation follows stable owner order; first rejection retains text, cursor, selection, focus, and result; Cancel bypasses content validation intentionally.
integrationSlices.negativeOrFallback: Help, application, and unknown commands remain open and unconsumed; invalid edit, focus loss, and acceptance are rejected atomically; Cancel remains the explicit fallback.
integrationSlices.helperRole: PrimaryProof: real dialog event handling and input mutation/focus paths execute; validators are production objects, not test replacements.
integrationSlices.proofLimit: This slice does not define application-specific dialog command lists or copy every historical validator subclass.
integrationSlices.platforms: Managed dialog and input behavior is platform-neutral after event normalization.
integrationSlices.a11yEvidence: Rejection is text-first, focuses the first invalid control, preserves entered state, and leaves Cancel keyboard-reachable.
integrationSlices.residualRisk: New completion commands or input mutation paths could bypass ordered validation.
integrationSlices.followUp: None for the current closed completion and validator contracts.
integrationSlices.reevaluationTrigger: Completion classification, child order, validator phase, input state, rejection text, or Cancel policy changes.

integrationSlices.title: Typed file outcomes, named resources, allowlisted reconstruction, and atomic rejection
integrationSlices.productionEntry: TFileDialog outcome classification and TResourceFile -> primitive UI record -> explicit Controls factory
integrationSlices.assertions: Every file mode returns a typed metadata outcome over test-owned paths; exact resource keys, versions, limits, primitive records, first-match order, commands, shortcuts, and rendered cells survive valid reconstruction.
integrationSlices.negativeOrFallback: Invalid path, wildcard, version, range, graph, truncation, trailing data, unknown type, duplicate key, and size limits reject atomically without history or object publication.
integrationSlices.helperRole: PrimaryProof: real file-dialog, resource parser, adapter, and Controls factories execute; temporary paths are setup-only fixtures.
integrationSlices.proofLimit: This slice performs no arbitrary user-file I/O, destructive operation, historical binary decode, or arbitrary runtime activation.
integrationSlices.platforms: Temporary owned paths run locally and in exact-head OS jobs; record parsing is platform-neutral.
integrationSlices.a11yEvidence: Invalid path feedback is text-first; reconstructed menu/status descriptions retain visible cells and accessible shortcuts.
integrationSlices.residualRisk: Callers own later I/O and future registrations could expand the allowlist.
integrationSlices.followUp: Revalidate before adding a file mode, persisted record, type registration, or parser limit.
integrationSlices.reevaluationTrigger: File outcome, path classifier, resource schema, parser bound, exact-key lookup, or UI factory changes.

consumerReadiness.flow: Application loop, menus, status, dialogs, help, mouse, idle refresh, dynamic commands, and window arrangement.
consumerReadiness.rationale: The shared input and command path is reusable; remaining mapped contracts are closed by later Feature-028 rows rather than local demo code.
consumerReadiness.residualRisk: Wave-specific clock, heap, and demo composition remain unimplemented and are not proof of a shared framework defect.
consumerReadiness.followUpBoundary: Feature 029 and its finding-derived closure must finish before Wave 5 can start.
consumerReadiness.reevaluationTrigger: TVDEMO consumer flow, a mapped shared contract, or a cited production proof changes.

consumerReadiness.flow: Editor windows, dialog execution, close/resize/next commands, and typed file decisions.
consumerReadiness.rationale: Existing desktop, close, command, dialog, keyboard, and typed file-outcome contracts cover the shared editor shell responsibilities without consumer-local substitutes.
consumerReadiness.residualRisk: Wave-specific editor composition and user-file policy remain unimplemented.
consumerReadiness.followUpBoundary: Feature 029 must close its own findings before Wave 5 may port this consumer.
consumerReadiness.reevaluationTrigger: Editor ownership, close, command, dialog, keyboard, or file-outcome contracts change.

consumerReadiness.flow: Named runtime resources for menus, status, dialogs, and visible UI composition.
consumerReadiness.rationale: Exact named lookup and allowlisted modern UI reconstruction provide the reusable behavior without historical binary-format parity.
consumerReadiness.residualRisk: Wave-specific resource content and composition still require consumer tests.
consumerReadiness.followUpBoundary: Use source-controlled modern descriptions during Wave 5; do not decode unchecked historical resources.
consumerReadiness.reevaluationTrigger: Named lookup, resource schema, allowlist, or UI reconstruction changes.

consumerReadiness.flow: Generated or described menu, status, dialog, and file-dialog resources.
consumerReadiness.rationale: The modern description and exact-key resource contracts replace the unsafe generator/binary coupling while retaining the historical composition intent.
consumerReadiness.residualRisk: A future generator could emit unsupported or unbounded records.
consumerReadiness.followUpBoundary: Wave 5 may generate only the closed allowlisted schema and must retain atomic rejection.
consumerReadiness.reevaluationTrigger: Resource generation, schema, parser bounds, or registered UI records change.

consumerReadiness.flow: Idle-updated visible gadgets and demo commands integrated with the application lifecycle.
consumerReadiness.rationale: Bounded idle ordering and shared command-state refresh cover the common framework role; gadget calculations remain consumer logic.
consumerReadiness.residualRisk: A Wave-specific gadget could perform unbounded work during Idle.
consumerReadiness.followUpBoundary: Each Wave-5 gadget must prove bounded work, visible state, and keyboard-reachable commands.
consumerReadiness.reevaluationTrigger: Idle scheduling, command refresh, or the related demo consumer set changes.

consumerReadiness.flow: Mouse interaction and settings dialog with complete keyboard operation.
consumerReadiness.rationale: Concrete mouse events, bounded capability handling, and keyboard parity provide the shared input boundary; Wave-specific settings remain local composition.
consumerReadiness.residualRisk: Historical timing and button-reversal settings are not a claim of native driver parity.
consumerReadiness.followUpBoundary: Feature 029 and the Wave-5 implementation must prove the selected terminal capability and keyboard fallback.
consumerReadiness.reevaluationTrigger: Mouse ingress, capability, keyboard fallback, or settings behavior changes.

consumerReadiness.flow: Named resources, idle refresh, shared commands, active-window broadcasts, and desktop arrangement.
consumerReadiness.rationale: Current lifecycle, desktop, command, keyboard, and resource contracts cover the file-manager shell without importing its Pascal ownership model.
consumerReadiness.residualRisk: The complete file-manager product composition and destructive policies remain unimplemented.
consumerReadiness.followUpBoundary: Feature 029 and Wave-5 closure precede the Wave-6 implementation and renewed delta audit.
consumerReadiness.reevaluationTrigger: File-manager shell lifecycle, commands, desktop, resources, or keyboard contracts change.

consumerReadiness.flow: Incremental directory scan during idle, tag broadcasts, and bounded drag/drop initiation.
consumerReadiness.rationale: Bounded idle, command refresh, and generic drag negotiation provide the shared mechanics; directory enumeration and copy policy remain product work.
consumerReadiness.residualRisk: Large directories can still create product-level scheduling and cancellation requirements.
consumerReadiness.followUpBoundary: Wave 6 must define bounded enumeration, cancellation, and operation policy without changing the shared gate silently.
consumerReadiness.reevaluationTrigger: Idle, command, drag, directory enumeration, or cancellation contracts change.

consumerReadiness.flow: Generic mouse tracking, drag presentation, target negotiation, and list-view drop mechanics.
consumerReadiness.rationale: The generic session owns threshold, capture, target, terminal result, and cancellation; item semantics remain consumer-owned.
consumerReadiness.residualRisk: New targets may require product-specific acceptance and accessibility policy.
consumerReadiness.followUpBoundary: Wave 6 must layer item and destructive-operation policy above the shared drag session.
consumerReadiness.reevaluationTrigger: Drag threshold, capture, target, cancellation, result, or keyboard parity changes.

consumerReadiness.flow: Focused tree child, file/tree window ownership, close-all, and desktop fallback.
consumerReadiness.rationale: Group focus, state-specific ownership, desktop stack, close outcomes, and fallback are reusable for tree windows.
consumerReadiness.residualRisk: Tree-model selection and file-system refresh remain Wave-specific.
consumerReadiness.followUpBoundary: Wave 6 must prove tree selection and refresh without bypassing group or desktop ownership.
consumerReadiness.reevaluationTrigger: Focus ownership, group state, desktop order, close, or tree-window lifecycle changes.

consumerReadiness.flow: Rename and attribute dialogs with ordered validation and typed file outcomes.
consumerReadiness.rationale: Completion classification, validator phases, state preservation, and typed file decisions cover the reusable dialog boundary.
consumerReadiness.residualRisk: Actual rename and attribute mutation policy is not part of the shared dialog contract.
consumerReadiness.followUpBoundary: Wave 6 owns authorization, conflict, rollback, and user confirmation for file mutations.
consumerReadiness.reevaluationTrigger: Dialog completion, input validation, file outcome, or mutation policy changes.

consumerReadiness.flow: Color dialog validation, preview, cancellation, and state restoration.
consumerReadiness.rationale: The existing dialog and input contracts provide acceptance, cancellation, rejection, and state-preservation mechanics; palette policy remains local.
consumerReadiness.residualRisk: High-contrast and palette semantics require separate product and A11Y acceptance.
consumerReadiness.followUpBoundary: Wave 6 must preserve keyboard operation and text-first rejection while defining palette behavior.
consumerReadiness.reevaluationTrigger: Dialog validation, input state, palette, or high-contrast behavior changes.

consumerReadiness.flow: Destructive copy, move, delete, and trash operations above the shared file and drag mechanics.
proofReferences: Feature-024 consumer review retains destructive file operations as a Wave-6 product-policy boundary.
consumerReadiness.rationale: The shared framework is ready to host the flow, but authorization, confirmation, conflict, rollback, and failure-recovery policy cannot be inferred from historical application code.
consumerReadiness.residualRisk: Premature porting could expose destructive operations without an accepted safety and recovery contract.
